subproblem.title: Area formula on an embedded C¹ submanifold for a C¹ map that is injective with injective derivative (Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.13, as used in 5.1–5.2)
subproblem.statement: Area formula on an embedded C¹ submanifold. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; M ⊆ ℝ^P; a Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P; a map Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Hypotheses: M is an embedded C¹ m-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M); E is Borel (MeasurableSet E) and E ⊆ M; Φ is C¹ on ℝ^P; Φ is injective on E; the derivative DΦ(x) = fderiv ℝ Φ x is injective for every x ∈ E. Notation: for x ∈ ℝ^P let T_x := span(tangentSpace M x) (a linear subspace, with the inner product of ℝ^P) and ι_x : T_x → ℝ^P the inclusion; J^MΦ(x) := √det((DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x)), where * is the adjoint for the inner products of T_x and ℝ^P and det is the determinant of the endomorphism (DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x) of T_x. Conclusion: H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m as an equality in [0, ∞], where H^m = μHE[m] and the integrand is read through ENNReal.ofReal (a lower Lebesgue integral ∫⁻ over E).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M E : Set (Euclid P)) (Φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M → MeasurableSet E → E ⊆ M → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → InjOn Φ E → (∀ x ∈ E, Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ x)) → μHE[m] (Φ '' E) = ∫⁻ x in E, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt ((((fderiv ℝ Φ x).comp (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)).subtypeL).adjoint ∘L ((fderiv ℝ Φ x).comp (Submodule.span ℝ (tangentSpace M x)).subtypeL)).det)) ∂μHE[m]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.13 (area formula on a submanifold through local representations and the Jacobian factorization J_{f∘ψ} = J_ψ·J^M_f of 4.11), as used in Ch. 2, 5.1–5.2 (H^n(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dH^n) and in step (0c) of the supplied proof of the parent. The Euclidean area formula used below is the kernel-checked SimonGMT theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Simon (3.2) for a map that is injective with injective derivative on a measurable set). Sibling lemmas: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv) and locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed).

Notation. H^m := μHE[m]. For a finite-dimensional real inner product space S and a linear map L : S → ℝ^P put J(L) := √det(L*L). The endomorphism L*L of S is positive semidefinite, so det(L*L) ≥ 0, and for every orthonormal basis s_1, …, s_k of S, det(L*L) = det(Ls_i·Ls_j)_{i,j} (a Gram determinant). J(L) is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet L (normDet_sq). With this notation J^MΦ(x) = J(DΦ(x)∘ι_x).

1. (Jacobian factorization, Simon 4.11.) Let A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be linear and injective with range R, and B : ℝ^P → ℝ^P linear. Then J(B∘A) = J(A)·J(B∘ι_R), ι_R : R → ℝ^P the inclusion.
 Proof. Write A = ι_R∘S with S : ℝ^m → R a linear isomorphism. Then A*A = S*S and (BA)*(BA) = S*(Bι_R)*(Bι_R)S. Computing determinants in orthonormal bases of ℝ^m and of R, det(S*CS) = det(S)²·det(C) for every endomorphism C of R. Hence det((BA)*(BA)) = det(S)²·det((Bι_R)*(Bι_R)) = det(A*A)·det((Bι_R)*(Bι_R)); take square roots. (This is also SimonGMT areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential and Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp.)

2. (Countable chart cover.) For each y ∈ M fix a chart (V_y, W_y, ψ_y) as in IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M: V_y ⊆ ℝ^m and W_y ⊆ ℝ^P open, y ∈ W_y, ψ_y C¹ and injective on V_y, ψ_y(V_y) = W_y ∩ M, V_y ∩ ψ_y^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W_y, and Dψ_y(v) injective for v ∈ V_y. By chart_tangent_space, tangentSpace M (ψ_y(v)) = range Dψ_y(v) for v ∈ V_y; this is an m-dimensional linear subspace, so T_{ψ_y(v)} = range Dψ_y(v). Since ℝ^P is second countable, the open cover {W_y}_{y∈M} of M has a countable subcover {W_k}_{k≥1}; let (V_k, W_k, ψ_k) be the corresponding charts. Put E_k := (E ∩ W_k) ∖ (W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_{k−1}). The E_k are Borel, pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_k E_k = E, because E ⊆ M ⊆ ⋃_k W_k.

3. (Each chart is a homeomorphism onto W_k ∩ M.) ψ_k is continuous and injective on V_k with image W_k ∩ M. If z_j ∈ V_k and ψ_k(z_j) → ψ_k(z) with z ∈ V_k, then K := {ψ_k(z_j) : j} ∪ {ψ_k(z)} is a compact subset of W_k, so all z_j lie in the compact set V_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(K); every cluster point z' ∈ V_k of (z_j) satisfies ψ_k(z') = ψ_k(z), hence z' = z; so z_j → z. Thus ψ_k^{-1} : W_k ∩ M → V_k is continuous.

4. (Pieces in coordinates.) Let F_k := V_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(E_k), a Borel subset of ℝ^m (ψ_k is continuous on the open set V_k). Since E_k ⊆ W_k ∩ M = ψ_k(V_k) and ψ_k is injective on V_k, ψ_k(F_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(B)) = E_k ∩ B for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^P.

5. (Euclidean area formula.) Let f be ψ_k or Φ∘ψ_k, and let F ⊆ F_k be Borel. At every v ∈ F (an interior point of V_k), f is differentiable with derivative Dψ_k(v), respectively DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v) (chain rule); both are injective, since Dψ_k(v) is injective and DΦ(ψ_k(v)) is injective (ψ_k(v) ∈ E). f is injective on F (ψ_k is injective on V_k, and Φ is injective on E ⊇ ψ_k(F)). By injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (with finrank ℝ^m = m; on ℝ^m the measure μHE[m] is Lebesgue measure L^m),
 (5.1) H^m(ψ_k(F)) = ∫_F J(Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v),
 (5.2) H^m(Φ(ψ_k(F))) = ∫_F J(DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v).

6. (Change of variables on E_k.) For every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫_{E_k} g dH^m = ∫_{F_k} g(ψ_k(v))·J(Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v). For g = 1_B (B Borel) this is (5.1) with F := F_k ∩ ψ_k^{-1}(B), by step 4. Both sides are additive and positively homogeneous in g, so the identity holds for nonnegative simple Borel functions, and by monotone convergence for every Borel g ≥ 0.

7. (J^MΦ is Borel on M.) For v ∈ V_k, step 1 with A := Dψ_k(v) (whose range is T_{ψ_k(v)}, step 2) and B := DΦ(ψ_k(v)) gives
 (7.1) J(DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v)) = J(Dψ_k(v))·J^MΦ(ψ_k(v)), with J(Dψ_k(v)) > 0.
 The maps v ↦ J(Dψ_k(v)) and v ↦ J(DΦ(ψ_k(v))∘Dψ_k(v)) are continuous on V_k (Dψ_k and DΦ are continuous, and Gram determinants are polynomials in inner products). By (7.1), v ↦ J^MΦ(ψ_k(v)) is continuous on V_k, so by step 3 J^MΦ is continuous on the relatively open set W_k ∩ M. As the W_k cover M, the restriction of J^MΦ to M is continuous. M is Borel (locally_closed, part (a)), hence g := 1_M·J^MΦ is a Borel function on ℝ^P, and g = J^MΦ on E.

8. (Area formula on E_k.) By (5.2) with F := F_k, by (7.1), and by step 6 applied to g:
 H^m(Φ(E_k)) = ∫_{F_k} J^MΦ(ψ_k(v))·J(Dψ_k(v)) dL^m(v) = ∫_{E_k} J^MΦ dH^m.

9. (Summation.) Each Φ(E_k) is Borel, because Φ is continuous and injective on the Borel set E_k (Lusin–Souslin; Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). The sets Φ(E_k) are pairwise disjoint because Φ is injective on E. Hence
 H^m(Φ(E)) = Σ_k H^m(Φ(E_k)) = Σ_k ∫_{E_k} J^MΦ dH^m = ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m,
 the last equality by countable additivity of E' ↦ ∫_{E'} g dH^m over the disjoint Borel sets E_k. Since J^MΦ ≥ 0, the right side is ∫⁻_E ENNReal.ofReal(J^MΦ) dH^m, and J^MΦ(x) is exactly √det((DΦ(x)∘ι_x)*(DΦ(x)∘ι_x)) with T_x = span(tangentSpace M x) (= tangentSpace M x for x ∈ M). This is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Jacobian factorization J(B∘A) = J(A)·J(B restricted to range A) for injective A (Simon 4.11).
Cover M by countably many charts and split E into disjoint Borel pieces E_k = ψ_k(F_k) inside chart domains.
Apply SimonGMT injective_area_formula_of_injective_derivative to ψ_k and to Φ∘ψ_k on F_k, and derive ∫_{E_k} g dH^m = ∫_{F_k} g∘ψ_k·J(Dψ_k) for Borel g ≥ 0.
J^MΦ is continuous on M (chart coordinates), so H^m(Φ(E_k)) = ∫_{E_k} J^MΦ dH^m.
Sum over k: the Φ(E_k) are Borel (Lusin–Souslin) and pairwise disjoint, giving H^m(Φ(E)) = ∫_E J^MΦ dH^m.
